Empirical Research Plan – “Do High-Value-Added (VA) Teachers Improve Students’ Long-Run Outcomes?”

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Phase 1 – Validation of VA measures  
• Event-study Difference-in-Differences (DID): compare (i) the same grade in a school in years just before/after a teacher arrival or departure and (ii) other grades in the same school-year as “within-school controls.”  
• The sharp timing of mobility shocks and the fact that all other inputs (principal, curriculum, peer pool) are unchanged at the moment of the move make an event-study the natural design.

Phase 2 – Impact of exposure on adult outcomes  
• Two-way-fixed-effects / within-school-by-grade-by-year design (“classroom randomization”): estimate  
    Y isg = β · VA_teacher + X′ γ + λ_sg + λ_sy + ε  
   where λ_sg are school-by-grade fixed effects and λ_sy are school-by-year fixed effects.  
• Instrumental-Variables robustness: use “arrival shocks” (mean VA change in grade g of school s in year t driven by inflow/outflow) as an instrument for actual teacher VA to reduce measurement error and residual sorting.

This two-step strategy directly speaks to (i) whether VA is a causal measure of contemporaneous achievement and (ii) whether that achievement translates into adulthood gains.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable  
• Main: Teacher i’s estimated value-added (VA_i) standardized to mean 0, SD 1 across NYC.  
• “High-VA teacher” = VA in top quartile (robustness: above +1 SD).

Control group / counterfactual  
• Students taught by lower-VA teachers in the same school-grade-year (for long-run regressions).  
• For the mobility event study the counterfactual is the same grade in the same school in years τ ≠ 0 relative to the move, and other grades in year 0.

Treatment timing / event date  
• τ = 0 is the first year a mobile teacher appears (arrival) or the first year after exit (departure). We estimate dynamic effects for τ ∈ {-4,…,+4}.

No running variable – not an RDD.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Conditional random assignment of students to classrooms within a school-grade-year.  
 • Plausible because NYC does not systematically sort students by prior achievement when assigning to elementary classrooms; we will verify balance on lagged scores.

A2. Parallel trends / no differential shocks at τ = 0 other than teacher move.  
 • In the short window (+/-2 yrs) schools rarely change curricula or principal; include school×grade and school×year FE to net out any remaining shocks.

A3. No anticipation and no re-sorting of students or teachers just before the move.  
 • Test by examining τ = -1 coefficients – expectation is zero.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): one teacher’s VA affects only her own students.  
 • Peer spillovers across classrooms are possible; we will include grade-level peer-mean prior score to soak up spillovers and show robustness to excluding multi-class grades.

A5. First stage relevance (for IV): teacher mobility generates large discrete changes in mean VA; confirmed in Phase 1.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification and Remedies
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Non-random assignment of higher achieving students to incoming high-VA teachers.  
  Remedy:  check pre-treatment covariate balance; control for lagged student score deciles and demographics; add classroom-level pre-treatment mean score as control.

T2. Other simultaneous school changes (new principal, restructuring).  
  Remedy:  include school×year FE; drop moves that coincide with principal changes as robustness; narrow event window.

T3. Measurement error in VA attenuating long-run effects.  
  Remedy:  (i) use Empirical Bayes (shrinkage) VA estimates; (ii) IV using mobility-induced mean-VA shocks; (iii) split-sample VA (estimate VA on pre-period, apply to post).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table); library(fixest); library(did); library(sandwich)

# ---- 1. Load data ----
stu  <- fread("students_1989_2009.csv")      # student-year observations
teach<- fread("teachers_va.csv")             # teacher IDs + VA estimates
map  <- fread("class_assignment.csv")        # stu_id, year, grade, teacher_id
mob  <- fread("teacher_mobility.csv")        # teacher_id, school_id, year, move_type

# ---- 2. Merge and construct variables ----
dt <- merge(map, stu, by = c("stu_id","year","grade"))
dt <- merge(dt, teach[,.(teacher_id, VA_std = VA_zscore)], by="teacher_id")
dt <- merge(dt, mob, all.x = TRUE,
            by = c("teacher_id","school_id","year"))
dt[, high_VA := as.integer(VA_std > 1)]                # top ~16%
setorder(dt, school_id, grade, year)

# Mean VA in each school-grade-year (needed for IV)
dt[, mean_VA_sgy := mean(VA_std, na.rm=TRUE), 
      by = .(school_id, grade, year)]

# Mobility shock: change in mean VA from t-1 to t due to arrivals/departures
dt[, delta_mean_VA :=
      mean_VA_sgy - shift(mean_VA_sgy, 1L, type="lag"),
      by = .(school_id, grade)]

# ---- 3. Event-study for test scores (Phase 1) ----
# Build event time relative to move (τ)
move_dt <- unique(mob[move_type %in% c("arrival","departure"),
                      .(teacher_id, school_id, grade, year, move_type)])
setnames(move_dt, "year", "move_year")

dt <- merge(dt, move_dt, by = c("teacher_id","school_id","grade"), all.x = TRUE)
dt[, rel_year := year - move_year]    # NA for non-mobile teachers

# Keep ±4-year window
es_dt <- dt[!is.na(rel_year) & abs(rel_year) <= 4]

fe_event <- feols(test_score ~ i(rel_year, ref = -1) | 
                   school_id^grade + school_id^year , data = es_dt,
                   cluster = ~school_id^grade)
etable(fe_event)

# ---- 4. Long-run outcome regression (Phase 2) ----
# Y: earnings age 25-32 (average, demeaned by cohort)
long_dt <- merge(dt, fread("adult_outcomes.csv"), by="stu_id")
long_dt <- long_dt[age %between% c(25,32),
                   .(earnings = mean(earnings_w2, na.rm=TRUE),
                     stu_id, school_id, grade, year, teacher_id, VA_std,
                     race, female, lag_score=lag_test_score)]

ols <- feols(earnings ~ VA_std + lag_score + race + female |
              school_id^grade + school_id^year, data = long_dt,
              cluster = ~school_id^grade)
summary(ols)

# IV using delta_mean_VA as instrument
iv <- feols(earnings ~ 1 | VA_std ~ delta_mean_VA |
            school_id^grade + school_id^year, data = long_dt,
            cluster = ~school_id^grade)
summary(iv)

# ---- 5. Robustness: restrict to students with balanced covariates ----
bal_dt <- long_dt[abs(lag_score - mean(lag_score)) < 1]
r_rob <- feols(earnings ~ VA_std + lag_score |
                school_id^grade + school_id^year, bal_dt,
                cluster = ~school_id^grade)
summary(r_rob)
```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Contemporaneous scores: A 1 SD increase in teacher VA should raise end-of-year
test scores by ≈ 0.10 SD (by construction of VA shrinkage).

Long-run: 1 SD higher teacher VA in a single grade is expected to raise annual
earnings at age 28 by roughly 0.5 % (≈ \$150 on \$30k mean), raise college
attendance by 1 ppt, and lower teen-birth probability by ~0.5 ppt.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Event-Study / DID)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Parallel trends (pre-τ flat) ………………… 1  
C2: No anticipatory sorting ………………………… 0.8  
C3: No simultaneous confounders ……………… 0.9  
C4: Consistent treatment (“dosage”) ………… 0.9  
C5: Correct inference / clustering …………… 1  
                        Average ≈ 0.92 → high internal validity.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
